name: SATA (data 7-pin + power 15-pin)
description: The storage interface on PC drives, split into two L-shaped keyed connectors: a 7-pin DATA connector (one transmit and one receive differential pair, each fenced by grounds) and a separate 15-pin POWER connector (3.3 V, 5 V, 12 V rails + grounds). This entry's contacts are the 7-pin data connector; the power connector is in the variants.
variants: POWER connector (15-pin): pins 1-3 = 3.3 V, 4-6 = GND, 7-9 = 5 V, 10 = GND, 11 = staggered activity/PWDIS, 12 = GND, 13-15 = 12 V. Three pins per rail carry the current; the connector is a separate L-key next to the data one.
eSATA is the same protocol on a ruggedized external connector (no power); SATA power adapters from Molex are common.
gotchas: Data is two differential pairs -- TX (A) and RX (B) -- each with a ground on both sides. It's point-to-point (one drive per port), not a bus.

PWDIS (power pin 3, the 3.3 V line on newer drives): SATA 3.3 spec makes pin 3 a power-disable. A Molex-to-SATA adapter (which has no 3.3 V) or taping pin 3 is the classic fix for a drive that won't spin up on a modern PSU.
Both connectors are keyed (the L notch) so they only insert one way -- but the thin edge tabs snap if you lever the cable sideways.
SATA is hot-pluggable if the port/OS support it; the longer ground pins mate first for safe hot-plug.
notes: SATA 7-pin data (GND/TX+/TX-/GND/RX-/RX+/GND). 15-pin power rails summarized in variants. PWDIS pin-3 gotcha included.
